headline: South Asia: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser.
- Africa: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Wave of Drone Strikes in War-Torn Sudan.
- Western Russia: Russian drone strikes home improvement superstore in Mykolaiv Oblast: two women injured.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Army support for Golden Dome missile shield takes shape.
- Military Times, 3 hours ago: US Army support for Golden Dome missile shield takes shape.
A U.S. Army air defense unit has been "earmarked" for support of the Golden Dome for America project, an Army official confirmed.
- Military Times, 6 hours ago: Marine Corps creates first medium missile battalion.
As the service's first medium missile battalion, the 1st Battalion, 10th Marine Regiment, will be equipped with NMESIS as a complement to its artillery.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, officials say.
Netanyahu and Hegseth discussed “the threats in the region” and the U.S.-Israel partnership in dealing both offensively and defensively with those threats.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Honourable finale - Vaz believes OJ membership perfectly timed to cap public service career.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: Honourable finale - Vaz believes OJ membership perfectly timed to cap public service career.
Certain that he is in the twilight of his political career, Transport Minister Daryl Vaz said his appointment to the Order of Jamaica (OJ) was perfectly timed and a fitting way to cap his life in public service. “The stars have aligned for me, and I could not want or ask for any better in terms of my leaving public service on the highest note possible,” he told The Gleaner after receiving the honour at yesterday’s annual National Honours and Awards Investiture Ceremony, held on the lawns of King’s House in St Andrew, where 140 Jamaicans were recognised.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 15 hours ago: MoBay mayor urges St James residents to uphold resilience post-Melissa.
WESTERN BUREAU: Ahead of the one-year anniversary of Hurricane Melissa’s devastating impact on western Jamaica, Montego Bay Mayor Richard Vernon is urging residents of St James to continually embody the resilience and determination that the parish displayed during and after the Category 5 hurricane’s October 28, 2025 passage. Vernon made the call on Monday while addressing St James’ National Heroes Day Civic and Awards Ceremony in Sam Sharpe Square, Montego Bay, held under this year’s theme ‘Resilient People with a Proud Heritage’.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russian drone strikes home improvement superstore in Mykolaiv Oblast: two women injured.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian drone strikes home improvement superstore in Mykolaiv Oblast: two women injured.
Two women have been injured as a result of a Russian drone attack on the Epicentr home improvement superstore in the city of Pervomaisk in Mykolaiv Oblast.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russia attacks Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology in Kyiv for second time – photos.
A Russian strike has hit the Strazhesko Institute of Cardiology in Kyiv for the second time, destroying an operating theatre and injuring one patient.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians strike energy facility in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast, injuring one.
One person has been injured in a repeat Russian attack on an energy facility in Ukraine's Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast on 20 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Zelenskyy: We are not losing the war.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Kyiv is ready for negotiations and any form of ceasefire, expressing hope that the US and European partners will help end Russia’s aggression as soon as possible.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Rubio insists the US isn’t trying to hurt Ukraine.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Rubio insists the US isn’t trying to hurt Ukraine.
The Ukrainian president complained about delayed air defense deliveries, the U.S. no longer warning of ballistic missile attacks and a slowdown in crucial Starlink services.
- Politico Europe, 3 hours ago: China threatens retaliation if UK follows the EU on tariffs.
China urged Britain to follow World Trade Organization rules and warned it against copying Brussels’ approach, arguing that tariffs on Chinese EVs would be discriminatory.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: Albanian PM Rama Steps Up Rhetoric Against Student Protesters.
Edi Rama described some of the student protesters involved in unrest in Tirana as extremists who have been manipulated by foreign powers, causing critics to warn that such harsh rhetoric may further inflame tensions.

AFRICA

- AllAfrica - Conflict, 16 hours ago: Sudan: UN Condemns Deadly Wave of Drone Strikes in War-Torn Sudan.
[UN News] Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.
- Africanews, 6 hours ago: Russia: Huge flames and smoke rise over St Petersburg after drone strikes.
Huge plumes of black smoke billowed over St Petersburg, Russia’s second-largest city, on Sunday, 18 October, as a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack sparked fires at industrial and logistics facilities. Russian officials said 126 drones had been intercepted in the surrounding region.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 11 hours ago: Nigeria: Military Air Strikes Neutralise 103 Terrorists in North-East.
[Vanguard] The Joint Task Force (North-East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), has reported the neutralisation of 103 terrorists and the destruction of several logistics hubs and storage facilities in seven precision air strikes conducted across its area of operations between October 10 and 18, 2026.

A 65-year-old woman has died after being attacked by a shark while swimming at a popular beach in South Africa's Eastern Cape province.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Netanyahu vows to eliminate Iran regime, sources tell 'Post' Trump 'very close' to renewing strikes.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Netanyahu vows to eliminate Iran regime, sources tell 'Post' Trump 'very close' to renewing strikes.
On Tuesday, Netanyahu described the Iranian regime as "so fanatical" that it will continue its nuclear ambitions and attempt to rebuild its terror proxy axis "as long as it lives."
- Jerusalem Post, just now: UK police re-arrest pair on suspicion of helping Iranian intelligence over RAF Fairford incident.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham last week said that the activity at RAF Fairford, which had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, was likely to have been coordinated in Iran.
- Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Pentagon deploys USS Theodore Roosevelt to Middle East as Trump weighs Iran strikes - report.
New US naval deployments to the Middle East could expand President Donald Trump's military options as his administration weighs additional strikes on Iran.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Jerusalem Daily: half a million Palestinians lose food aid.
Israeli strikes kill Palestinians in Gaza as funding shortages threaten food aid for half a million people
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Two Dead, Three Seriously Injured in Bindura Mine Blast.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 8 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Two Dead, Three Seriously Injured in Bindura Mine Blast.
[263Chat] Two people have been killed and three others seriously injured in a blasting accident at Goldry Mining Syndicate in Bindura, police have confirmed.

ASIA

- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser.
Adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) and former director general of the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) retired Lieutenant General Mazhar Jamil has warned of the “risky” outcome for South Asia and beyond of a “dangerous ideology” shaping the Indian military mindset. “Indian military thinking is being shaped by a dangerous ideology, which conflates mythology with national power.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks.
British fighter planes will be deployed to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels, the UK government announced on Tuesday. The defence ministry said the deployment formed part of “additional defensive military support” to Riyadh. “The UK will fly defensive counter air missions to support the protection of Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure against aerial attack, using RAF Typhoon fighter jets,” the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said in a statement.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 9 hours ago: Rubio says India made 'substantial progress' in diversifying oil purchases.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday that India had made “substantial progress” in diversifying its energy supplies, including away from its key importer, Russia. “What India has expressed repeatedly is their desire to diversify their energy portfolio, which is a smart thing to do,” Rubio said on a visit to India’s economic capital, Mumbai.
- The Hindu - International, 4 hours ago: Death toll rises to 60 in Houthi strike on Yemen training camp in deadliest attack in months.
At least a dozen people were still missing a day after the Iran-backed rebels hit the al-Alam training camp in Shabwa province with ballistic missiles, Yemeni officials said

Within seconds, an explosion rang out from a tanker ahead. “That was traumatic for me when I saw that the tanker ahead of our vessel had been hit,” said Jay, whose real name has been withheld to protect him from possible employer retribution. Gen. Jennie Carignan, Canada’s chief of the defense staff, said in an exclusive interview in Seoul that North Korea’s […]

Seoul warned that it would “resolutely punish” any further “provocations” by North Korea on Tuesday, pushing back against a Kim Yo Jong statement threatening to restart border loudspeaker broadcasts. India - bottom line: 'Russia is a big machine': Trump says Ukraine 'has to want' to settle war with Putin.
- Times of India - Top Stories, NDTV - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Russia is a big machine': Trump says Ukraine 'has to want' to settle war with Putin.
US president Trump pointed to Russia's ability to sustain its military campaign and capture territory, portraying Moscow as having the upper hand in the conflict. "Russia is a big machine - they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land," he said.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 10 hours ago: Kerala man gets Rs 54,500 payout after cruise cancelled without notice.
A family's dream cruise was abruptly canceled without warning, leaving them in distress. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kerala found both the holiday company and cruise operator at fault. Despite repeated attempts to secure a refund after the cancellation, the complainant was denied compensation. The commission mandated a refund along with additional compensation for the trouble caused, allowing one month for compliance before penalties escalate.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Man Shot Dead In Manipur, Days After Killing Of 3 Firewood Collectors.
The man was heading towards a forested area to collect bamboo shoots when unidentified people opened fire.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: Delhi BJP leader burns cockroach effigy; Dipke responds with SRK’s 'Swades' song.
During Dussehra celebrations in Delhi, a 30-foot cockroach effigy was burned alongside traditional effigies of Ravan. Organizers stated that the effigy symbolized filth and promoted cleanliness in line with health awareness initiatives. Leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party reacted sharply, suggesting the move provided them with free publicity. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra remarked that cockroaches symbolize chaos and filth, reflecting public sentiment.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Helen Haines live updates: Alleged attacker Brendan Nugent to face court in Wangaratta this morning.

Speaking to AAP, Hutchison shared her distress for Helen Haines and also recalled her personal experience of “a sustained, organised harassment and bullying campaign”.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: Australian MP Helen Haines attacked with car: what we know so far - The Latest.
A man has been charged after the Australian MP Helen Haines was allegedly attacked with a car outside her electorate office in the state of Victoria. Haines, who is an independent MP, has lost one leg as a result of the incident and surgeons were fighting on Tuesday to save the other leg. Police say 43-year-old Brendan Nugent has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a commonwealth public official.
